status_reasoning: Reviewers explicitly affirm the core modeling approach, stating 'the authors have answered the question of whether immune selection can cause the parasite population to self-organise into a finite number of strains with non-overlapping var repertoires even when the genes are expressed sequentially.' The agent-based model extending strain theory to var genes is accepted without methodological critique.

Reviewers accept that immune selection structures the parasite population into dominant repertoires with constrained diversity, noting the model shows 'the parasite population to self-organise into a finite number of strains.' The finding of punctuated turnover is acknowledged as 'a dynamically different process' without challenging its validity, though reviewers request clarification about the mechanism (Comment 2).

Reviewers explicitly affirm this finding, stating 'They have further shown that the degree of structuring depends on transmission intensity: partially overlapping repertoires can arise when transmission levels are high.' This represents a key theoretical advance that reviewers accept without challenge.

The model predictions about epidemiological signatures at different transmission intensities are implicitly accepted. Reviewers do not question these findings but instead request speculation about their implications for disease vs. infection (Comment 3), indicating acceptance of the underlying results.

Reviewers explicitly accept the empirical findings, stating the paper 'presents an analysis of microsatellite and var DBLα sequence data, revealing that linkage disequilibrium among the latter cannot be attributed to demographic forces alone.' This affirms the key empirical support for immune selection structuring var diversity.

While reviewers accept the observation of punctuated turnover, they express uncertainty about its mechanism, asking 'To what degree does the sequential expression itself contribute to this phenomenon?' and whether 'this behavior likely to be observed in a stochastic multi-locus model without sequential expression' (Comment 2). This indicates the finding is accepted but its interpretation requires clarification.

Reviewers challenge the interpretation that model insights explain difficulty of malaria elimination, stating 'It is not obvious that "This important insight provides a plausible explanation for why it is so difficult to eliminate malaria"' (Comment 3). They request speculation on differential effects on disease vs. infection, indicating the practical implications are not yet convincingly established.

Reviewers request discussion of how the model performs under non-lifelong immunity assumptions, citing 'recent evidence that malaria may well kill adults as well as children (Dhingra et al, Lancet 2010)' (Comment 4). While the model with lifelong immunity is not rejected, reviewers indicate uncertainty about its robustness to this assumption.

Reviewers note 'Parts of the Materials and methods are difficult to follow and parameters such as nh are not always clearly defined' and question notation choices and mathematical formulations (Comment 5). While not rejecting the model structure, reviewers indicate the methods require clarification for proper evaluation.
